book_vs_repo_gap: This appendix is faithful in core dynamic programming and EM mechanics, but it still lacks a multi-sequence training loop and supervised tagging bridge.

chapter_notes.counterintuitive_insight: Hidden states are not inherently identifiable. The valuable object is the posterior structure and likelihood, not a human-friendly state name.
covered_claims: Appendix A now includes forward-backward and one Baum-Welch update step.
Posterior marginals are exposed directly instead of only best-path decoding.

failure_modes.note: Equivalent latent-state permutations can preserve likelihood, so named hidden states should not be over-interpreted.

lesson_objectives: Run forward-backward to obtain posterior marginals in an HMM.
Show how one Baum-Welch step changes model parameters.
Separate latent posterior reasoning from best-path decoding.
title: Hidden Markov Models
